candidates.change_summary: Replace the condition msg.value >= MinDeposit with msg.value > MinDeposit, so deposits exactly equal to MinDeposit are rejected.
Delete the require statement that checks for overflow, allowing wrapping behavior on overflow to corrupt balances.
Replace balances[msg.sender]+=msg.value with balances[msg.sender] = msg.value, overwriting balance instead of adding.
Insert a second addition of msg.value to balances, doubling the deposit amount.
Replace the entire if condition with true, so deposits of any amount (including zero) are accepted.
Delete the entire if condition block, so Deposit always updates balances regardless of msg.value.
Replace require condition with true, effectively removing the overflow check.
Delete the require statement that checks for overflow, making the function vulnerable to integer overflow which could revert on large deposits instead of silently failing.
Replace 'msg.value >= MinDeposit' with 'msg.value > MinDeposit', changing the condition so that a deposit exactly equal to MinDeposit is rejected.
Replace 'balances[msg.sender]+=msg.value' with 'balances[msg.sender] = msg.value', changing the balance update to overwrite instead of increment.
Delete the entire if-condition block, so that deposits are never recorded in balances or logged.
Remove the balance check `if(_am<=balances[msg.sender])` so CashOut always proceeds regardless of balance, allowing underflow or zero transfer.
Change `balances[msg.sender] = (balances[msg.sender] - _am);` to `balances[msg.sender] = (balances[msg.sender] + _am);` so balance increases instead of decreasing on cash out.
Remove the ETH transfer `(bool _veri_ok,) = msg.sender.call{value: _am}("");` so balance is deducted but no ETH is sent.
Replace `balances[msg.sender] = (balances[msg.sender] - _am);` with `balances[msg.sender] = 0;` so that the entire balance is wiped instead of subtracting only the requested amount.
Delete the line `balances[msg.sender] = (balances[msg.sender] - _am);` so the balance is never deducted, but Ether is still sent.

Replace `(bool _veri_ok,) = msg.sender.call{value: _am}("");` with `(bool _veri_ok,) = address(this).call{value: _am}("");` so Ether is sent to the contract itself instead of msg.sender, yet balance deduction still occurs.
